analysis:
All changes are documentation only. No source or security-control code was changed in the supplied units.

- `docs/developer/test.md` (last-updated stamp 2026-10-15): reviewed the full head text. It documents tests for endpoint resumption, logout, App Attest dispatch, worker suites, native qualification, SSD cache gates and model-publication workflow checks. It consistently states these are synthetic or loopback tests, that the physical Apple gates are not replaced, and that production state must not be touched. No new attack surface or weakened assumptions found. Cache-related text (SSD write budget, encryption and no-fallback checks) is consistent with T-041.
- `docs/operations/model-migration.md`: new step 1 permits reusing an already-published valid upload without R2 write credentials. Registration text changed from the coordinator verifying hashes to the coordinator validating identity, inventory and sizes, with providers verifying hashes at download. This is the only finding, a low-severity threat-model gap on T-012/T-027, and the backend change behind it is unconfirmed (platform-owned).
- `docs/operations/model-revisions.md`: metadata only, with no patch or text supplied. The new anchor `model-revisions.md#choose-the-operation-first` and its access rules could not be reviewed. This is a coverage limit, so the next pass should check them if the content becomes available.

findings.detail: The head text of `docs/operations/model-migration.md` (lines 142-145) now says `HandleRegisterModel` only validates manifest identity and inventory and checks listed file sizes. It adds that 'Providers verify the actual file hashes when downloading.' The base text (lines 137-138) said the coordinator verified every listed file's existence, size and hash. If this reflects a real backend change, publication-time integrity checking has moved from the trusted coordinator to adversarial providers. A bad or tampered CDN/R2 object, or a manifest that does not match the files, would then be caught only on provider devices. A malicious provider (ADV-001) can skip that check and serve substituted weights (T-012, T-027, A-004). The new step 1 text also lets operators reuse already-published files without re-upload. Nothing in the supplied threat model records that the coordinator stopped checking hashes. Update the weight-substitution threats and mitigations to state the new verification point. Also state that the registered manifest hashes remain the trust anchor for provider downloads. If the hash check was removed unintentionally, restore it. The backend code is out of scope here, so this is unconfirmed.
findings.title: Registration docs now say the coordinator no longer verifies file hashes; the model-integrity threats are not updated
